reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in applying the Rao-Blackwell theorem to field goal percentage estimation. Standard FG% is a sample mean of Bernoulli trials, inherently noisy due to small sample sizes per player. By conditioning on shot trajectory data, the Rao-Blackwellized estimator (RB-FG%) reduces variance through the law of total expectation. The shot-make probability model serves as a bridge between spatial data and probabilistic outcomes, using optical tracking to extract entry angle, depth, and accuracy. These features are then mapped into a probability space via a learned function. The resulting RB-FG% estimator is a posterior expectation over these probabilities, yielding a more stable proxy for shooting skill. The Beta-Bernoulli model formalizes the uncertainty in individual shot outcomes, treating each shot as a draw from a Bernoulli with a latent probability drawn from a Beta distribution. This allows for principled inference of true shooting ability even with limited observations. The failure mode arises when trajectory data is absent or mislabeled, reverting to standard FG% with higher variance. The method also assumes that shot trajectory features are predictive of outcome, which may not hold in all contexts.
